title: Submersible Pump Pipe Installation Checklist for Borewell Projects
metaTitle: Submersible Pump Pipe Installation Checklist | Prayag
description: Use this submersible pump pipe installation checklist to verify borewell depth, pump HP, pipe size, pressure class, joints, handling and commissioning.
bannerAlt: Submersible pump pipe installation checklist for a borewell using uPVC column pipes
bodyHtml:
What should a submersible pump pipe installation checklist include?

A reliable submersible pump pipe installation checklist should confirm the borewell depth, pump HP, pipe size, pressure class, thread or joint design, lifting load, water condition and service access before the pump is lowered. These checks matter because the column pipe carries both water pressure and the suspended load of the pump assembly. For buyers comparing options, Prayag's uPVC column pipe range provides a relevant starting point, but the final choice should always be matched to the actual borewell and pump specification rather than selected by price or diameter alone.

Why borewell pipe selection must start before installation day

Many borewell problems begin before the first pipe is joined. A contractor arrives with a pump, the available pipe is accepted because it is close to the required size, and the installation proceeds without a written check of depth, pressure or joint type. The system may operate initially, yet the mismatch can later show up as joint stress, difficult pump retrieval, unstable flow or premature service work.

A better process treats the rising main as part of the pump system. The pump, column pipe, joint design, cable, delivery line and borewell geometry should be reviewed together. This is especially important in India, where residential, agricultural and commercial borewells can differ significantly in depth, daily operating hours and maintenance conditions.

1. Confirm the borewell depth and installation depth

Borewell depth is one of the first numbers that should be written down, but total drilled depth is not always the same as the final pump-setting depth. The installer should confirm where the pump will actually sit, how much pipe will be suspended, and how much head the system must overcome. These values influence the load carried by the column pipe and the pressure conditions during operation.

If the buyer is still deciding between pipe types or classes, Prayag's uPVC column pipe buying guide for submersible pumps and borewells is a useful related reference. It helps separate general product selection from the installation-specific checklist covered here.

2. Match the pipe to pump HP and operating duty

Pump HP is useful, but it should not be treated as a standalone pipe-selection rule. Two pumps with the same nominal HP can operate at different heads, discharge rates and duty cycles. Agricultural pumps may run for long stretches, while domestic borewell pumps may cycle for shorter periods. The installation team should therefore consider pump output, expected head, starting and stopping frequency, and daily runtime together.

Where an installer relies only on a familiar HP-to-pipe-size shortcut, the specification can miss other important conditions. A practical checklist records the pump model, discharge requirement and expected operating range so the selected pipe and joints can be checked against the actual system.

3. Choose the correct pipe size for flow and fitment

Pipe size affects more than physical fit. If the rising main is too restrictive for the intended discharge, friction loss increases and the pump can work against a less efficient system. If the pipe is oversized without a clear reason, the project may add cost and installation complexity without solving the real hydraulic requirement.

The borewell casing, pump outlet, delivery line and available fittings should be considered together. The installation should also leave enough practical clearance for lowering and future retrieval without forcing the pipe against the borewell wall.

4. Verify the pressure class instead of assuming all column pipes are the same

Pressure class is a critical selection point because column pipe systems operate under changing pressure as the pump starts, runs and stops. The required class should be chosen from the actual installation conditions and current product data. Prayag also has a dedicated guide to uPVC column pipe classes, which can be used when the buyer needs more detail on class differences before the final order is placed.

Do not select a higher class automatically as a substitute for engineering the system. The useful objective is to match the pipe to the borewell depth, pressure condition and pump duty with a suitable safety margin based on the applicable product guidance.

5. Check the joint, thread and connection system

A strong pipe can still perform poorly if joints are mismatched, damaged or tightened incorrectly. The installer should inspect threads or jointing surfaces before lowering the assembly and should reject pieces with visible damage, contamination or deformation. Components from one connection system should not be mixed casually with another simply because the nominal size appears similar.

The team should also agree on the assembly sequence before the pump is lowered. This is particularly important when several lengths are joined at the borewell mouth, where one damaged thread or poorly aligned connection can become difficult to correct once the assembly is suspended.

6. Decide between coupler-type and belling-type arrangements based on the system

The supplied draft identifies coupler-type and belling-type column pipe variants as relevant options. The installer should use the system specified for the project and ensure that all mating components are compatible. The decision should consider handling, jointing method, available accessories and the manufacturer's installation guidance.

Changing joint style mid-project because a different piece is available at the dealer can introduce unnecessary uncertainty. A simple material schedule prepared before installation keeps the pipe lengths, joints and related accessories consistent.

7. Inspect every pipe length before lowering the pump

Check for visible cracks, impact damage, distorted ends or damaged threads.

Make sure pipe interiors are clean and free from construction debris.

Confirm the printed/marked product specification matches the approved order.

Separate any damaged length rather than attempting an on-site compromise.

Keep sealing and jointing surfaces clean while the assembly is prepared.

Protect pipe ends from dirt and accidental impact before use.

Inspection is faster and cheaper on the surface than after the assembly is inside the borewell. The site team should therefore treat incoming material inspection as part of installation, not merely as a storekeeper's task.

8. Plan pump lowering, lifting and handling safely

The suspended assembly can become heavy, especially in deeper borewells. Handling should be planned so that the pipe is not dragged, sharply bent or allowed to strike the borewell edge. The lifting method should also protect the pump cable and avoid transferring unintended load to electrical connections.

Competent installers should use appropriate handling equipment for the depth and pump weight. The purpose of the checklist is not to replace site safety procedures, but to ensure that pipe selection and installation planning account for the real lifting load instead of focusing only on water pressure.

9. Keep the pump cable and pipe routing organised

Cable management should be planned as the pipe assembly is lowered. Poor routing can cause abrasion, pinching or difficult retrieval. Cable supports should follow the pump manufacturer's and installer's approved practice, with enough care to prevent the cable from rubbing against rough surfaces.

The pipe, cable and any other borewell components should descend without twisting into an uncontrolled bundle. A tidy installation improves commissioning checks and future servicing.

10. Review water condition and site environment

Water quality and borewell conditions vary considerably across India. Sediment, hardness and site cleanliness can influence maintenance frequency and the condition of connected equipment. The buyer should disclose known water conditions to the installer and follow product guidance for the intended use, particularly where the water is used for drinking or sensitive process applications.

For a wider view of how borewell piping connects with other site plumbing, Prayag's plumbing solutions page is useful when planning the downstream line, storage and distribution system.

11. Plan the delivery line and above-ground connection

The installation does not end at the borewell head. The rising main connects to the delivery arrangement, which may feed a storage tank, irrigation line or building supply. Sudden reductions, poorly supported transitions or mismatched fittings can create stress near the top of the borewell.

If the project also uses other plastic piping systems, review the intended application before mixing materials. Prayag's broader uPVC pipe range is a separate category from uPVC column pipe and should be selected for the appropriate above-ground or distribution use rather than treated as an interchangeable borewell rising main.

12. Test the system before treating the job as complete

Commissioning should confirm that the pump starts and runs as expected, the delivery flow is stable, joints remain dry, and abnormal vibration or movement is absent. Electrical checks remain the responsibility of the competent pump/electrical installer, while the plumbing inspection should confirm that the rising main and delivery connection are behaving normally.

The installer should document pump details, pipe specification, approximate setting depth and any important site observations. Those notes are valuable when the pump is serviced later because the maintenance team does not have to reconstruct the original installation from memory.

uPVC column pipe vs GI pipe: what should buyers compare?

Material choice is another common borewell question. Rather than assuming one material is universally better, compare weight, handling, corrosion exposure, jointing, installation method, service access and the project specification. Prayag's detailed uPVC column pipe vs GI pipe comparison covers that material decision separately.

For this installation checklist, the main rule is consistency: once the system is selected, every pipe length, joint and accessory should follow the approved design and current manufacturer's guidance.

Common installation mistakes to avoid

Ordering pipe before confirming the actual pump-setting depth.

Choosing only by pump HP without checking head, discharge and pressure class.

Using the closest available pipe size instead of the approved size.

Mixing incompatible joints, couplers or connection styles.

Ignoring visible thread or end damage because installation has already started.

Allowing pipe or cable to drag across rough ground during lowering.

Failing to plan future pump retrieval and service access.

Treating the above-ground delivery connection as an afterthought.

Skipping commissioning notes and leaving no record of the installed specification.

Why Prayag can be considered for borewell column pipe projects

The supplied Prayag draft positions the brand around lead-free uPVC column pipes, coupler-type and belling-type options, pressure-class variants and rising-main applications for submersible pumps. It also describes Prayag as an established Indian bathware and plumbing brand with a broad connected product portfolio and nationwide channel presence. Those factors can make product availability and category planning easier for buyers who prefer to source related plumbing products within one ecosystem.

Brand strength, however, should not replace specification. Even when a buyer chooses Prayag, the final pipe size, class and joint system should still be checked against the actual pump and borewell conditions.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the most important check before installing a submersible pump pipe?

Confirm the actual pump-setting depth, pump model and operating requirement before finalising the pipe. These inputs influence size, class, suspended load and installation planning.

Can pipe size be selected only from pump HP?

Pump HP is useful, but it should be considered with head, discharge, outlet size, borewell geometry and the manufacturer's product guidance.

Why does pressure class matter in a borewell?

The rising main operates under pressure that varies with depth and pump operation. The selected class should cover the intended service conditions according to current product data.

Should I choose uPVC column pipe or GI pipe?

Compare project conditions rather than relying on a universal rule. Weight, corrosion environment, handling, joints, service needs and the approved pump system all matter. See Prayag's uPVC column pipe vs GI guide for a focused comparison.

When should the installation checklist be completed?

Complete the main specification checks before ordering and repeat the physical inspection before the pump is lowered. Waiting until installation day increases the chance of accepting a mismatched or damaged component.

Where can I review Prayag column pipe options?

Start with the Prayag uPVC column pipe category and confirm the final selection with the project installer or supplier using the current product specification.

Final recommendation

A good borewell installation is the result of several small checks being completed in the correct order. Confirm depth, pump duty, pipe size, pressure class and joint system before material is ordered; inspect every length before lowering; protect the assembly during handling; and document the final installation for future service. Following that sequence reduces last-minute substitutions and makes the pump system easier to maintain over its working life.
